summary: Bryce Ryan worked in Indology and other fields. He held posts at the University of Ceylon and Cornell University, and he taught Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah.

Bulcsu Siklós specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of London under doctoral supervisor Tadeusz Skorupski and teacher Charles R. Bawden, and held a post at SOAS University of London (attested 1996).

Bunga Fukui studied Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies at Waseda University and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Paul Demiéville, Maxime Kaltenmark, and Rolf Alfred Stein. He later served as a professor at Waseda University (~1978–2005).

Bunkyo Aoki specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University and as a disciple of Kozui Otani (~1910–1914), later serving as a Tibetan language lecturer at the University of Tokyo in 1951, succeeding Tokan Tada.

Bunsaku Kurata studied at Aoyama Gakuin and Waseda University, working in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He served in the Tokyo National Museum, the National Commission for Protection of Cultural Properties, and became Director of Nara National Museum in 1975.

Bunyiu Nanjio was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology who studied at Otani University and Oxford under Friedrich Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He held posts at the University of Tokyo and Otani University, serving as its director.

Bunzaburo Matsumoto studied at the University of Tokyo and worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He held professorships at Rikkyo University, First Higher School, and Kyoto University (1906–1929), later directing Kyoto University's Institute for Research in Humanities in 1938.

Burchard Brentjes worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg under Heinz Mode, subsequently holding a post there from ~1954 to 1978 and succeeding Mode in 1978.

Burkhard Quessel is a Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg. He was a member at the University of Hamburg (attested 1997) and served as a curator at the British Library (attested 2002–2012).

Burton Stein was an historian and Indologist. He held posts at the University of Hawaiʻi (~1969–1988) and SOAS University of London (~1983–1996), where he was a Professorial Research Associate in the Department of History.

Burton Watson studied at Columbia and Kyoto universities under L. Carrington Goodrich, Chi-chen Wang, and Wm. Theodore de Bary. He worked in Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies, holding posts at Kyoto, Columbia, and Stanford University.

C. D. Sebastian works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD from Banaras Hindu University, had postdoctoral mentorship from Paul Williams and Gavin D'Costa, and became Professor of Indian Philosophy at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay.

C. Kunhan Raja, an Indologist and philosopher, earned a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford. He served as the University Professor and Head of Sanskrit at the University of Madras and as Honorary Director of the Adyar Library and Research Centre.
C. Peter Bankart is a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields. He held a post at Wabash College (attested 2003) and was a visiting researcher at Dartmouth College.

C. R. Krishnamacharlu worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Madras Christian College and Pachaiyappa's College, and held a post at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1925–1943).
C. S. Srinivasachariar was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held professorships at Pachaiyappa's College and Annamalai University (attested 1932–1933).
C. S. Sundaram was an Indology scholar who held posts at Madras Sanskrit College and the University of Madras, where he became Reader in Sanskrit in 1951. He taught Tomy Augustine.

C. W. Huntington, Jr. worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez and Madhav M. Deshpande, and served as a professor at Hartwick College (~1992–2020).

Calambur Sivaramamurti studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri at Presidency College, Chennai, working in Indology and archaeology. He held posts at the Government Museum in Chennai, the Indian Museum, the Archaeological Survey of India, and the National Museum, New Delhi.

Calvert Watkins studied linguistics and Indology at Harvard, the EPHE, and DIAS. He was a professor of linguistics and classics at Harvard (1959–2003) and later a distinguished professor in residence at UCLA (2003–2013).
